summary: This exact version establishes a sufficient spectral recovery criterion for finite Boolean Doob chains with matched marginals and bounded stationary second moment. Four disjoint column families with sublinear rank loss control the entire ordered spectrum. A second theorem permits a fixed multiplicative neighbourhood of a structured reference law. I recommend circulation as a working paper. This is a first author-side AI assessment in shared context.
strengths: Pages 2–3 track the codimension losses even when each family spans a different subspace. The gain from the rare set is (3/4)(1/21)=1/28.

Pages 4–5 control the logarithmic change of the potential in stationary L^p and recover an estimate for arbitrary ambient test vectors. The identity 1/84+20/21+1/28=1 yields the stated exceptional-set power.
The two examples compute the intrinsic deficit. In the perturbed example the character differences generate each singleton although the reference has rank one.
weaknesses: The factor 33 on the rank defect and width 1/4096 are sufficient bounds. The paper does not determine their optimal values or how large the unspecified constant is for a given second moment.
The last section controls deterministic observable moments in a common Gram representation. Applying this to measurements in stationary coordinates would require an additional transport estimate.
Several references appear as inline links with little bibliographic information in print. The embedded PDF Title and Author metadata are empty, although both are clearly printed on the first page.
potential_errors: A direct application of quotient hypercontractivity to the perturbed signed weight would be unjustified. On page 5 the argument instead dominates its absolute value by a positive quotient envelope and cancels the low-degree part using the actual matching; this resolves the concern.
A subcode localized on few coordinates need not produce a slowly mixing chain. The implication on pages 2–4 is expressly necessary and the examples respect that direction.
strong_novelty_candidates: A necessary support-versus-dimension obstruction for persistent discrepancy of Boolean Doob spectra, derived from a four-family rank deficit.
Fixed-width relative perturbation stability with full ambient Walsh span and without a dimension-uniform positive floor.
